nodes.content: Design an incremental cross-module optimizer that preserves optimization benefits while maintaining sound cache reuse under symbol interposition.
requirements: Match clean-build semantics under dependency changes, dynamic symbol interposition, and mixed optimized/unoptimized modules.
For single-module edits, halve full-LTO rebuild time while keeping runtime within 5% of full LTO.

nodes.content: Cache imported IR by dependency digests, symbol-resolution maps, and optimization modes; selectively reoptimize dependents while preserving preemptible calls.
Which visibility and symbol-binding changes invalidate cached imported IR, and which leave preemptible calls safe to reuse?
Per-symbol fingerprints covering visibility, version, and prevailing definition invalidate dependent imports; unchanged dynamically bound calls match clean builds.
Enumerate ELF binding transitions; compare fingerprint-triggered invalidation against clean builds under LD_PRELOAD, dependency edits, and mixed optimization modes.
Run InterposeMatrix-120 binding-transition cases across dependency edits, mixed modes, and LD_PRELOAD; compare incremental outputs and traces against clean builds.
InterposeMatrix-120 produced 0 trace mismatches versus clean builds; fingerprint changes invalidated affected imports, while unchanged preemptible calls remained reusable.
Adopt per-symbol binding fingerprints and preserve preemptible calls; InterposeMatrix-120 found zero clean-build trace mismatches.
InterposeMatrix-120 report archives clean/incremental traces, binding-fingerprint transitions, and imported-IR invalidation decisions for all 120 cases.
Seed a 500-case binding-transition fuzzer from the InterposeMatrix-120 report; compare fingerprint invalidations and preemptible-call traces against clean builds.
Removing -Bsymbolic left fingerprints unchanged; 3/500 incremental traces bypassed LD_PRELOAD while clean builds interposed.
Fingerprints including -Bsymbolic state and call-site binding assumptions invalidate stale direct calls when symbol interposition becomes possible.
Implement -Bsymbolic and call-site binding fingerprints; rerun 500 fuzz cases and 200 binding toggles against clean builds.
Expanded fingerprints invalidated all three stale direct calls; 700 fuzz and binding-toggle cases showed zero clean-build trace mismatches.
Which imported-function summaries need recomputation after one module changes, and which cached inlining decisions remain profitable?
Binding-aware fingerprints permit recomputing changed summaries and transitive consumers while retaining unaffected inlining within 5% of full-LTO runtime.
Prioritize profile-hot cross-module imports in bounded ThinLTO partitions; retain indirect calls for preemptible symbols and treat unoptimized modules conservatively.
Profile-rank imports, cap ThinLTO partitions, benchmark single-module edits, and tune for ≤50% rebuild time and ≤5% runtime regression.
Derive single-module edit workloads from InterposeMatrix-120 report's invalidation records; benchmark profile-hot partition caps against full-LTO rebuild and runtime.
EditBench-120 dataset records per-edit rebuild seconds, runtime ratios, partition caps, and full-LTO baselines for report-derived workloads.
Audit EditBench-120 rebuild/runtime ratios against 50%/5% targets and InterposeMatrix-120 trace coverage; identify missing interposition transitions.
EditBench-120: all 120 edits rebuilt within 49% of full-LTO time and 4.8% runtime regression; InterposeMatrix-120 covered no -Bsymbolic removals.
Adopt profile-hot partitions with expanded binding fingerprints: EditBench-120 meets both targets, and 700 binding tests match clean-build traces.
Run MixedMode-90 mixed-mode dependency edits and LD_PRELOAD tests; compare cached profile-hot partitions with clean-build traces and full-LTO rebuild/runtime.
MixedMode-90: cached IR misbound 2/90 unoptimized providers; conservative profile-hot partitions matched all traces, rebuilding in 47% of full-LTO time.
Which linker-resolution metadata must profile-hot partitions record to avoid stale bindings when unoptimized providers replace optimized ones?
Partition keys covering prevailing provider, optimization mode, symbol version, and -Bsymbolic-derived preemptibility eliminate MixedMode-90 misbindings.
Implement provider/mode/version/preemptibility keys; rerun MixedMode-90 and EditBench-120, checking trace parity, transitive invalidation, and retained-inlining runtime ≤105% full-LTO.
Expanded keys eliminated both MixedMode-90 misbindings, but retaining unaffected inlining yielded 6.3% EditBench-120 runtime regression versus full LTO.
Fuzz 400 provider swaps, symbol-version changes, and -Bsymbolic toggles; compare keyed partition reuse against clean-build symbol-resolution traces.
In 2/400 MixedMode-90-derived version swaps, default-alias flips reused unversioned imports despite unchanged keys, diverging from clean-build traces.
Include default-version alias mappings in partition keys to invalidate unversioned imports after alias flips.
Add default-alias mappings to partition keys; replay 400 provider/version/binding swaps and MixedMode-90 against clean-build resolution traces.
Alias mappings left 2/400 mismatches; refreshing stale linker-resolution snapshots updated existing symbol-version keys and eliminated both without alias mappings.
With refreshed linker snapshots, ablate default-alias keys across 400 swaps and MixedMode-90; compare invalidations and clean-build traces.
After snapshot refresh, alias-key ablation exposed a different unversioned-import mismatch (1/400); restoring alias keys yielded 0/400.
Are refreshed linker snapshots and default-alias keys both required to prevent distinct version-swap misbindings?
Both are necessary: refreshed snapshots invalidate changed version resolutions; default-alias keys invalidate unversioned imports when aliases flip.
Run a four-configuration ablation of snapshot refresh and default-alias keys on 400 swaps, checking both prior misbindings against clean-build traces.
Execute 2×2 snapshot-refresh/default-alias-key ablation over 400 provider swaps; record clean-build trace mismatches by versioned versus unversioned import.
Across 400 swaps, trace mismatches were 3 with neither safeguard, 2 alias-only, 1 refresh-only, and 0 combined.
BindingAblation-400 report tabulates four safeguard configurations, versioned/unversioned mismatch IDs, refreshed snapshot hashes, and clean-build trace diffs.
Combine refreshed linker snapshots and alias-aware cache keys with selective reinlining of hot transitive consumers in bounded partitions.
Which hot transitive consumers should be reinlined to cut EditBench-120's 6.3% runtime regression below 5% without exceeding 50% rebuild time?
Reinlining changed-summary consumers covering 80% of sampled cross-module call time reduces runtime regression below 5% within 50% rebuild time.
Sweep hot-consumer coverage from 50% to 90% on EditBench-120; measure per-edit rebuild ratio, runtime regression, and clean-build trace parity.
Sweep 50–90% hot-consumer coverage on EditBench-120, using BindingAblation-400 mismatch IDs to verify trace parity and measure rebuild/runtime ratios.
HotSweep-120 table records 50–90% consumer-coverage settings, per-edit rebuild/runtime ratios, and BindingAblation-400 trace checks.
Audit HotSweep-120’s 80% coverage results across all edits for ≤50% rebuild time, <5% runtime regression, and zero trace mismatches.
At 80% coverage, HotSweep-120’s worst edit rebuilt in 49% of full-LTO time, regressed runtime 4.7%, and matched all traces.
Compare p2 and p3 on EditBench-120/HotSweep-120 edits, measuring worst-case rebuild/runtime ratios and clean-build trace parity.
Cold-cache edits: p2 rebuilt in 49% of full-LTO time; p3 needed 55%, despite 4.7% runtime regression and trace parity.
Rebenchmark p2 on EditBench-120 using p3’s 55%-time cold-cache edits; measure rebuild ratio, runtime regression, and clean-build trace parity.
On p3’s cold-cache edits, p2 rebuilt in 49% of full-LTO time but regressed runtime 6.3%, exceeding the 5% limit.
Can cold-cache reinlining be limited to the highest-impact consumers while meeting both 50% rebuild and 5% runtime limits?
Reinlining highest-impact consumers covering 60% of sampled call time keeps cold-cache rebuilds ≤50% and runtime regression <5%.
Sweep 40–70% hot-consumer coverage on the identified cold-cache edits, comparing rebuild/runtime ratios and traces with full LTO.
Extend HotSweep-120 to EditBench-120 cold-cache edits; test 40–70% coverage against full-LTO rebuild/runtime and clean-build traces.
At 60% coverage, cold-cache edits rebuilt in at most 50% of full-LTO time, regressed runtime 4.9%, and matched clean-build traces.
Adopt 60%-cold/80%-warm reinlining with conservative mixed-mode bindings; cold edits meet 50% rebuild and 4.9% runtime regression, unlike alternatives.
Use transactional binding snapshots and a content-addressed import graph to reuse safe partitions with 60%-cold/80%-warm reinlining.
How can transactional snapshots detect linker-resolution changes during concurrent cache reads without invalidating unaffected import-graph partitions?
On snapshot-epoch changes, revalidate version-alias-aware binding hashes at commit; invalidate only partitions importing changed resolutions.
Implement epoch-pinned reads and commit-time binding-hash checks; stress concurrent relinks with validated 60%-cold reinlining and selective invalidation.
Build ConcurrentRelink-300 from BindingAblation-400 cases; race provider/version swaps against partition reads, logging epochs, hash changes, invalidations, and traces.
ConcurrentRelink-300 log records pinned/commit epochs, per-import binding hashes, invalidated partitions, and clean-build trace comparisons for 300 races.
Audit ConcurrentRelink-300 for stale trace commits and unnecessary invalidations, grouping races by changed binding hash versus epoch-only change.
ConcurrentRelink-300: zero stale trace commits; 41 epoch changes invalidated 17 affected partitions while preserving 24 unaffected ones.
Inject 100 relinks between commit-time hash validation and artifact publication; compare published traces with fresh-link clean builds.
In 4/100 post-validation relinks, artifacts published under stale epochs and diverged from fresh-link clean-build traces.
Publish artifacts under an exclusive epoch lock spanning final binding-hash validation through atomic rename, retrying only changed-import partitions.
Add publication locking, replay 100 post-validation relinks plus ConcurrentRelink-300, and measure trace parity, selective retries, and rebuild overhead.
Implement epoch-locked atomic publication; replay ConcurrentRelink-300 and 100 post-validation injections, measuring stale traces and retried partitions.
ConcurrentRelink-400 supersedes the 300-race log, adding publication-lock intervals, atomic-rename epochs, partition retries, and clean-build trace comparisons.
Audit ConcurrentRelink-400 for published trace mismatches, unnecessary retries, and lock-held durations versus the 50% rebuild budget.
ConcurrentRelink-400 had zero trace mismatches, including 100 injected relinks; 24 unaffected partitions stayed cached, with 1.2 ms p95 locks.
Audit ConcurrentRelink-400 publication epochs against fresh-link builds, isolating relinks queued during the lock and checking post-unlock artifact reuse.
In 2/400 queued relinks, provider files changed before rename while epoch updates waited; published artifacts diverged from fresh-link builds.
Gate provider-file writes with publication locking and recheck content digests before rename, retrying partitions whose inputs changed.
Integrate provider-write gating and pre-rename digest checks; replay queued relinks, verify clean-build traces, and bound lock overhead.
Gate provider writes under publication locks, check digests before rename, and replay ConcurrentRelink-400 plus 100 queued-write injections.
ConcurrentRelink-500 supersedes the 400-case log with queued-write timestamps, pre-rename digests, lock intervals, retries, and fresh-link trace comparisons.
Audit ConcurrentRelink-500 for queued-write trace mismatches and digest-triggered retries; compare p95 lock time with the 1.2 ms baseline.
ConcurrentRelink-500: zero fresh-link trace mismatches; two digest-triggered retries, with p95 lock time rising from 1.2 to 1.8 ms.
Compare ConcurrentRelink-300/400/500 for queued-write trace parity, unnecessary invalidations, and lock overhead against p4’s 50% rebuild target.
ConcurrentRelink-500 eliminated the 400-case log’s two queued-write mismatches (0/500), retained 24 unaffected partitions, and rebuilt in 49.9% of full-LTO time.
Adopt write-gated, digest-checked publication: 0/500 mismatches versus lock-only races, with rebuild time 49.9% of full LTO.
How can cache reuse detect external linker-script edits and unmanaged provider writes that bypass publication locks?
Fix the adopted 60%-cold/80%-warm configuration and write-gated publication baseline; hash linker inputs and test unmanaged writes against clean builds.
Hash linker inputs; inject unmanaged provider and linker-script edits into EditBench-120, HotSweep-120, ConcurrentRelink-500; compare p2/p3/p4 clean-build traces and rebuild/runtime ratios.
Hashed-input p2/p4 had 0/120 unmanaged-edit trace mismatches; p4 rebuilt in 49.9% full-LTO time with 4.9% runtime regression.
Choose hashed-input p4 over p2/p3: write-gated publication and 60%-cold/80%-warm reinlining achieve 0/120 mismatches, 49.9% full-LTO rebuild time, 4.9% runtime regression.
